headline: Ex-airman Tahsif Souri found dead in Turag river, friend in custody
summary: PBI is investigating the death of Tahsif Souri, a former air force officer, after his body was recovered from the Turag river.
details: Tahsif Souri, a former air force officer, was found dead in the Turag river. His family has alleged that he was murdered, while PBI is investigating the possible causes of death.
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) is suspecting that Tahsif may have been strangled before being dumped in the river. They are also probing potential links to local or foreign syndicates.

A friend of the victim, identified as Dwip, is currently in PBI custody for questioning. During interrogation, Dwip reportedly stated that Tahsif jumped into the river after being chased by some unidentified people.
A motorcycle without a license plate, which was used by Tahsif, used to be found in the Mazar slum area near the river.
Authorities are currently verifying the ownership of the motorcycle to gather more evidence and as part of the ongoing investigation into the death.
The investigation continues as PBI works to determine whether this was a suicide or a planned murder involving a syndicate.
caption:
A former air force officer found dead in the Turag river. Was it a suicide or a planned murder?

Tahsif Souri, a former air force officer, was found dead in the Turag river. His family has alleged that he was murdered, while PBI is investigating the possible causes of death.

The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) is suspecting that Tahsif may have been strangled before being dumped in the river. They are also probing potential links to local or foreign syndicates.

A friend of the victim, identified as Dwip, is currently in PBI custody for questioning. During interrogation, Dwip reportedly stated that Tahsif jumped into the river after being chased by some unidentified people.

A motorcycle without a license plate, which was used by Tahsif, used to be found in the Mazar slum area near the river.

Authorities are currently verifying the ownership of the motorcycle to gather more evidence and as part of the ongoing investigation into the death.

The investigation continues as PBI works to determine whether this was a suicide or a planned murder involving a syndicate.

headline_marked: New rules: [[Registration mandatory for e-rickshaws]] in city corporations
headline: New rules: Registration mandatory for e-rickshaws in city corporations
summary: Battery-powered rickshaws are now barred from highways and expressways, with registration fees up to Tk 10,000.
details: The government has made registration mandatory for battery-powered rickshaws operating in city corporation areas. New regulations, the Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Operated Rickshaw (E-Rickshaw) Movement Rules, 2026, took effect yesterday.
Under the new rules, e-rickshaws are strictly barred from operating on highways, expressways, and major bus routes across all city corporations in Bangladesh.
City corporations, in consultation with traffic authorities, will now determine the number of permitted e-rickshaws and designate specific operating zones, routes, and vehicle colours.
A vehicle registered in one city corporation or zone will not be allowed to enter another. This ensures localized control over the number of vehicles on the road.
Registration fees are set at Tk 8,000 for two-passenger vehicles and Tk 10,000 for four-passenger vehicles. Annual renewal fees are Tk 4,000 to Tk 5,000, and fitness certificates cost Tk 1,000.
All e-rickshaws must comply with technical and safety standards prescribed by BUET. Existing vehicles may be approved if they undergo necessary structural modifications and pass fitness inspections.
The rules aim to regulate the movement and safety of these low-speed vehicles to reduce congestion and improve urban transport management.
